design.provenance_note: ecc.tools brand_extract.py ran confidence=low (heuristic frequency guess, no confirmed CSS variables); falling back per routine step 6.2/6.3 to the 'claude' preset -- earned rather than arbitrary, since the project IS Everything Claude Code.

provenance.accent: claude preset terracotta, deepened further (#CC785C -> #8B4226) so the flash beat's accent-filled background reads unambiguously dark for the polarity-aware readability gate, while still clearing accent/canvas contrast well above the 3.0 floor

readability.accent_is_graphic_not_text: raw #CC785C stays on dots/fills/strokes; --accent-ink (accent blended toward black to ~60 luma) used for any accent-colored hero text so it doesn't wash out on cream
readability.muted_content_rule: activity lines / detail rows use --muted-content (muted blended toward ink); ink_muted stays for decorative-only whispers

per_scene_light_source.1_title: hero wordmark in full ink weight fills ~70% of frame width -- the light source IS the type mass
per_scene_light_source.2_stack_hackathon: bold ink numerals (8 hours / $15k) at hero scale against paper
per_scene_light_source.3_diagram: diagram nodes/rules in ink with one terracotta accent node lit as the through-line; midground rule-lines carry the plate
per_scene_light_source.4_terminal: mono_block/terminal pane on a subtly darker paper plate so typed ink text keeps contrast while accent tags the prompt
per_scene_light_source.5_sparkline: sparkline drawn in accent, end-dot glow, big_number count-up in full ink -- brightest, busiest frame in the piece
per_scene_light_source.6_flash_inverted: INVERTED beat: near-black field, cream/ink-on-dark hero word -- the one polarity flip, contrast budget spent here
per_scene_light_source.7_quote: pull-quote in ink at hero scale, thin rule underneath
per_scene_light_source.8_close: wordmark rhymes with scene 1 composition for the autoloop

readability.inverted_beat: scene 6 (flash) flips to a dark field so the piece isn't one flat cream wash for 29s
